description: InjectionHunter findings reviewed and accepted, each with the reason it is not an injection. Read by tools/Invoke-TPSecurityAnalysis.ps1: a finding not listed here fails the build, and an entry nothing matches fails as stale. Matched by path, rule and the first line of the flagged code (whitespace collapsed), with a count. Add an entry only after reviewing the code; fixing the code is better.

entries.Reason: Instance property read on the Exchange connection object; $p iterates the literal list 'TenantId','TenantID','TenantGuid' and is checked with PSObject.Properties.Match first. No input chooses the name.

Loads the two MSAL assemblies shipped in the installed Microsoft.Graph.Authentication module's Dependencies folder (fixed file names joined to the module's own ModuleBase). No source code is compiled; whoever can write that module folder already runs code as the operator.
Reads one registry value by name from Get-ItemProperty's own result; $Name is the value name the calling check passes as a literal. No input chooses the name.
Instance property read on an authentication-method object; $fld iterates the literal list 'displayName','phoneNumber','emailAddress' and is checked against PSObject.Properties first.
Reads one group of findings from the publisher's own grouping; $section iterates the literal list 'Critical','High','Notes','Satisfied'.
Turns HTML line breaks into newlines and strips tags for Markdown text; nothing is quoted for a parser, and the result is escaped by the Markdown publisher before output.
Reads one group of findings from the publisher's own grouping; $section iterates the literal list 'Critical','High','Notes','Satisfied'.
Get-SafeProp, an instance property read inside try/catch; every caller passes the property name as a literal string. No tenant data chooses the name, and no static member is reachable through it.
Reads one certificate record by key from the collector's own TLS map; $role iterates that map's own keys (the probe roles the collector wrote).
Reads a clients.json record field; $declName iterates the literal list 'ThirdPartyEDR','ThirdPartyAwareness' and is checked with PSObject.Properties first.
The banner's record-field reader; every caller passes the field name as a literal ('Profile','ThirdPartyEDR','ThirdPartyAwareness') and it is checked with PSObject.Properties first.

The repository's one quoting rule for generated PowerShell: the value has already been refused if it holds U+2018..U+201B, a line break or separator, NUL, or a control or format character, so doubling the ASCII apostrophe is complete. TP.PsLiteral.Tests.ps1 parses the emitted script to prove it.

OData string escaping for a Graph $filter (the OData rule is doubling the apostrophe); $pat iterates the literal list 'Break Glass','BreakGlass','Emergency Access','EmergencyAccess'. No input reaches it.
Validates controls.json rows; $field iterates the literal list of required field names and is checked with PSObject.Properties first.

Quotes a value for a printed administrator command after refusing U+2018..U+201B, U+0085/2028/2029, line breaks and every control or format character, so doubling the ASCII apostrophe is complete; TP.DistributionListRemediation.Tests.ps1 pins the command grammar.
Undoes the data-file quoting to compare the round-tripped CompanyName with what was written; the result is only compared, never parsed or executed.

Quotes the legacy DN for Get-Recipient -Filter by doubling the ASCII apostrophe; the identifier is refused first if it holds U+2018..U+201B or any control, format or line-separator character, so no other quote character can end the value (TP.ExchangeTruth.Tests.ps1).
OData string escaping for the duplicate-app check's Graph $filter (the OData rule is doubling the apostrophe); $DisplayName is the operator's own parameter, and the query is read-only.
Reads one connection flag; $svc iterates the literal list 'Graph','EXO','IPPSSession','Teams','SharePoint'.
